question_text: What is the name of the anatomical delineation that separates the attached gingival from the alveolar mucosa?
explanation:
Mucogingival junction

	B.	Located at or approximately 0.5 mm coronal to the cemento-enamel junction (CEJ)
	C.	Nonkeratinized epithelium that surrounds and attaches to the tooth on one side and attaches on the other side to the gingival connective tissue
	D.	Mucogingival junction

	D.	Typically the widest area of attached gingiva

question_text: Nonbiofilm-induced gingivitis can be caused by a lack of which vitamin?
explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency can cause scurvy-related nonbiofilm-induced gingival bleeding and ulceration due to impaired collagen synthesis in capillary walls and gingival connective tissue.

question_text: What is the most accurate measure of severity of periodontal disease?
explanation:

	B.	Calculus plays a secondary role in the etiology of periodontal diseases by serving as a plaque-retentive factor
	C.	Clinical attachment level
	D.	Assessment of the patient’s homecare but not indicative of amount of periodontal destruction
